intro.title: Longest Common Subsequence
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function to find the longest common subsequence (LCS) between two strings, a classic algorithm problem. You will learn the core concept of dynamic programming, which solves complex problems by breaking them into simpler overlapping subproblems. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, arrays, and loops to implement the LCS algorithm efficiently. By the end, you will understand how to compare sequences and extract the longest shared subsequence without the characters needing to be contiguous.
intro.usecase: The Longest Common Subsequence algorithm powers practical text comparison features in developer tools and collaborative applications. You'll find it in code diff viewers like GitHub's file comparison, where it highlights the longest matching sequences between file versions. It also drives document revision tracking in Google Docs and Microsoft Word, showing what content was preserved versus changed. In bioinformatics, it helps compare DNA sequences to identify genetic similarities across species.
